# SQL query built from HTTP request data (Node.js)

`qualor:js/sql-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
SQL text built from HTTP request data (Express, Fastify, Next.js) and run through:

- `query()` or `execute()` of a node-postgres (`pg`) or `mysql2` connection, pool or client made in
  the same file, or of any object when the text visibly starts as SQL; also their query-config
  objects (`{ text }`, `{ sql }`);
- Knex `raw()` and the other raw-SQL methods of the query builder;
- Prisma's `$queryRawUnsafe()` and `$executeRawUnsafe()`;
- Sequelize `query()` and `literal()`, and TypeORM `query()`.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
When a value is pasted into SQL text, the database cannot tell it from the query. A value such as
`' OR '1'='1` changes what the query selects; others read other tables, change or delete data, or
on some databases run commands on the database server.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the customer name is concatenated into the query.

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const { Pool } = require('pg');

const app = express();
const pool = new Pool();

app.get('/orders', async (req, res) => {
  const { rows } = await pool.query(
    "SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE customer = '" + req.query.customer + "'",
  );
  res.json(rows);
});
```

**Compliant:** the value is a bound parameter.

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const { Pool } = require('pg');

const app = express();
const pool = new Pool();

app.get('/orders', async (req, res) => {
  const { rows } = await pool.query('SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE customer = $1', [
    req.query.customer,
  ]);
  res.json(rows);
});
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the SQL text constant and pass values separately: `query(text, values)` with `$1` (pg) or
  `?` (mysql2) placeholders.
- Use the query builder or ORM methods, which bind values: Knex `where()`, Prisma's model API or
  `$queryRaw` as a tagged template, Sequelize `where` conditions.
- In Sequelize `literal()`, quote values with `sequelize.escape()`.
- For identifiers (a column to sort by), choose from a fixed allow-list.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- Next.js
- Fastify
- node-postgres (pg)
- mysql2
- Knex.js
- Sequelize
- Prisma
- TypeORM

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- `query()`/`execute()` on a connection made in another module (`require('./db')`) is reported only
  when the query text visibly starts as SQL; otherwise it is missed. This keeps use-case objects,
  GraphQL clients and other `query()` methods out.
- Sources are Express-style handlers `(req, res, ...)`, Fastify handlers, Next.js Pages Router API
  routes and App Router route handlers (`GET`, `POST`, ... and their `params`). NestJS parameter
  decorators (`@Param()`, `@Query()`, `@Body()`) and Next.js `headers()`/`cookies()` are not
  sources.
- Handlers are recognised by the name of their second parameter (`res`, `reply`, `ctx`, `next`,
  ...): a handler written as `(request, out)` is not checked, and a one-parameter callback passed
  to `get()`/`post()` after a path is taken for a Fastify handler, also on HTTP clients.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test files [`rules/js/sql/sql-injection.js`](../../../rules/js/sql/sql-injection.js) and [`rules/js/sql/sql-injection.ts`](../../../rules/js/sql/sql-injection.ts) hold every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/js/sql/sql-injection.yml`](../../../rules/js/sql/sql-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.0.
